D.t: Jack Reed leads by 36.3 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 154,557 votes; a one point swing is about 2,130 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +29.4 and D +43.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +33.9. Your best recent poll is Emerson College/WPRI at D +34.6; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +20.3. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Providence, a projected net 82,807 votes; Washington, a projected net 22,762 votes; Kent, a projected net 20,692 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jack Reed runs furthest behind in Washington, Newport. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Voters who can afford daily costs, 37% of voters, 53 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 1.86 points; Economy voters, 35% of voters, 58 to 34, where a 5 point gain is worth 1.74 points; Other issue voters, 32% of voters, 56 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 1.57 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Jack Reed: Immigration voters 32 to 61, Voters who can afford daily costs 53 to 40, 2024 voters who skipped 2022 56 to 37. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
